purpose: Apache Kafka documentation promotion and bounded topic-partition offset-window reconciliation.

overrides.reason: Promote the existing Apache Kafka target from discovery to documentation-backed, read-only partition-window reconciliation without granting offset-commit, topic, producer, checkpoint, payroll or attendance authority.

connectionRoutes: Native Apache Kafka protocol through an exact customer-approved broker endpoint set
TLS or SASL over TLS using deployment-specific mTLS, SCRAM, GSSAPI or OAuth bearer identity
Customer-managed private networking, proxy or edge route where the cluster is not publicly reachable
Managed Kafka-compatible services remain separately versioned provider variants even when they share the Kafka protocol
readRoutes: beginningOffsets and read_committed endOffsets for exact approved partitions
seek to the approved beginning offset, poll bounded batches, and inspect final consumer position
cluster metadata and topic configuration reads required to bind cluster, topic UUID, partition, retention and compaction evidence
deniedMutationRoutes: automatic or manual consumer offset commits
topic create, delete, partition expansion or configuration changes
ACL, credential, quota, broker, replication or cluster configuration changes
stableIds: exact topic name and Kafka topic UUID plus partition plus arbitrary-precision offset
WFM tenant plus connection plus consumer-group identity
topic-metadata, topic-configuration, schema, mapping, source-scope and broker-endpoint-set fingerprints
patch.freshness: Kafka record timestamps are preserved as source evidence but are not assumed to be unique or causal. The authority binds an explicit observation horizon and broker beginning/end offsets for each partition, then proves the consumer position reached the bounded starting end offset.
permissions: Use an isolated read-only principal limited to metadata and consumer fetches for explicitly approved topics
Require encrypted transport; plaintext broker and SASL_PLAINTEXT routes are not admitted
Disable automatic offset commits and do not call commitSync, commitAsync or group offset mutation APIs
Keep topic administration, production, transactions, group resets and security administration outside the WFM reader
paginationAndDelta: Kafka polls are bounded pages within one exact topic-partition offset window
Manual partition assignment prevents dynamic rebalancing from silently changing the approved partition set
Beginning and read_committed end offsets are captured before reading; the final consumer position must equal the bounded end
The ending beginning offset must not advance and the ending end offset must not move backwards; concurrent appends beyond the bounded end remain for a later window
Numeric offset gaps are valid for compacted topics, transaction markers and aborted transactions and must not be fabricated as missing business records
patch.customFields: Kafka record keys, headers and payloads are schema- and customer-defined. The authority stores only approved decoded schema/mapping fingerprints and whole-record payload digests; raw credentials and unapproved payload data are rejected.
regionalAndVersionNotes: Pin the exact cluster id and customer-approved endpoint-set fingerprint; do not infer regions from hostnames
Pin Kafka client/broker compatibility, topic configuration, schema registry subject/version where used, and security mechanism
Self-managed Apache Kafka, Confluent, Amazon MSK, Azure Event Hubs Kafka endpoints and other compatible services require distinct provider overlays and evidence
Keep consumption and evidence storage in the customer-approved region and treat cross-region replication as a separate source identity
patch.rateLimits: No universal poll, fetch or metadata rate is assumed. Bound partitions, poll pages and records; honour broker throttling, request timeouts and quota errors; use backoff with jitter and stop on authentication, authorization, cluster, topic, schema or watermark drift.
failureModes: wrong cluster, topic, partition, consumer group or endpoint set
dynamic assignment or rebalance changing partition ownership
retention advancing the beginning offset during a bounded read
log truncation or leader failure moving an end watermark backwards
read_uncommitted exposure to aborted transactional records
consumer position stopping before the bounded end
duplicate offset replay with a conflicting payload digest or timestamp
schema, mapping, topic configuration or source-scope drift
offset overflow or precision loss in runtimes that coerce offsets to floating-point numbers
offset commit occurring before downstream reconciliation
reconciliation: Bind every read to the exact WFM tenant, connection, cluster id, topic, consumer group, secure transport, principal, schema, mapping and source scope
Use arbitrary-precision decimal strings for every broker and record offset
Require the exact approved partition set, stable beginning watermark, non-regressing end watermark and final position equal to the bounded end
Preserve increasing record order per partition, collapse byte-equivalent replays at one topic-partition offset and quarantine conflicts
Allow documented offset gaps without inventing records or declaring data loss solely from non-consecutive offsets
Emit only a reconciliation candidate; a later compare-and-swap process may consider checkpoint movement after downstream delivery proof
patch.schemaDrift: Pin topic configuration, raw/decoded record schema and mapping fingerprints. Quarantine unknown serialization, schema-registry identity drift, header/key semantics changes, topic recreation under the same name, partition expansion or security/version changes until reviewed.
retryAndRecovery: Retry transient polls only inside fixed partition and offset boundaries with bounded backoff
On authentication, authorization, cluster, topic, partition, retention, truncation or schema drift, abandon the candidate and re-observe before retrying
Exact replay of one offset may collapse only when timestamp type, timestamp and whole-record payload digest match
Never reset or commit group offsets as an automatic recovery action
After an outage, resume from the last independently approved WFM checkpoint and establish fresh broker watermarks
patch.evidenceNote: Official Apache Kafka documentation was reachable on 2026-09-27 and supports partition-scoped offsets, distinct current and committed positions, manual assignment, beginning/end watermarks, read_committed last-stable-offset behavior, valid offset gaps, secure authentication and topic retention/compaction configuration. No Apache Kafka cluster, managed Kafka tenant, customer authentication, live read, ACL denial, outage recovery, hosted proof or production certification was executed.
valueOpportunities: Reuse one event-stream path across ERP, MES, maintenance, quality, access, IoT, energy, logistics and workforce sources instead of bespoke point-to-point polling
Scale from one low-volume topic to thousands of partitions while preserving per-partition ordering, replay isolation and regional ownership
Detect retention loss, truncation, partial reads and conflicting replays before incomplete data reaches schedules, payroll preparation or operational decisions
Correlate manufacturing events with shifts, skills, labour cost and outcomes while preserving source time, lineage and non-causal boundaries
Reduce outage recovery time by retaining exact cluster/topic/partition/offset windows and failure diagnostics without mutating provider offsets
patch.nextBuildAction: In an authorised non-production Kafka cluster, authenticate a least-privilege read-only principal, manually assign two test partitions, capture read_committed beginning/end watermarks, consume to the bounded end without committing offsets, and reconcile duplicates, compaction gaps, aborted transactions, retention movement, broker interruption, partition expansion, schema drift and an exact-offset payload conflict.
